correctness.rationale: For induced matchings in rook graph K_m square K_n, each selected row-oriented edge uses 1 dedicated row and 2 dedicated columns, while each column-oriented edge uses 2 dedicated rows and 1 dedicated column. Inducedness means all row coordinates from distinct selected edges and all column coordinates from distinct selected edges are disjoint, so h+2v<=m,2h+v<=n are necessary and sufficient. Choose h rows, v columns, pair and assign remaining 2v rows to column edges and 2h columns to row edges. This bijection yields m!n!/[h!v!2^(h+v)(m-h-2v)!(n-v-2h)!]. Summing z^(h+v) gives full polynomial for every positive m,n including singleton dimensions. These inequalities imply k=h+v<=m,n,floor((m+n)/3); choose h=max(0,2k-m), v=k-h to realize k=min(m,n,floor((m+n)/3)). The equivalent object is vertex-disjoint P3 (two-edge) packing in K_{m,n}, via rook graph=L(K_{m,n}); the exact factorial profile is the count of such packings. Independent exhaustive enumeration of induced matchings on all 16 boards m,n<=4 reproduces every coefficient, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The rook graph is a canonical graph (Hamming graph H(2,m,n)), and its induced-matching polynomial counts every conflict-free edge selection by size, beyond a single optimum. The rectangular boundary and exact maximum min(m,n,floor((m+n)/3)) are complete, useful invariants that can serve as exact benchmark instances for induced-packing enumerators; a natural self-contained fact need not yield a broader theorem.
